hooks.text: This planet is darker than asphalt and glows red.
Orbiting just two million miles from its star, a planet is dying.
A doomed gas giant is being eaten alive by its parent star.

title: The Dark Planet Being Eaten Alive
description: Discover WASP-12b, a pitch-black gas giant trapped in a deadly death spiral around its host star.

beats.text: Discovered in 2008, the hot Jupiter known as WASP-12b whips around its star in roughly twenty-six hours.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a hot Jupiter exoplanet orbiting close to a star

beats.text: The exoplanet orbits just two million miles from its host, locking one side in permanent day.
beats.visual: Diagram of an exoplanet transit and light curve, NASA

beats.text: Enormous tidal forces have stretched this swollen world into a distorted egg shape.
beats.visual: Planet Jupiter full disk showing scale comparison, Hubble global view, 2014

beats.text: Dayside temperatures soar to over forty-six hundred degrees Fahrenheit, thermalizing the atmosphere so no clouds can form.
beats.visual: Spitzer Space Telescope in space artist concept, NASA
queries: Spitzer Space Telescope in space NASA

beats.text: Hubble observations revealed that its superheated gas is actively spilling onto the star.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope orbiting above Earth, STS-125, 2009
queries: Hubble Space Telescope above Earth orbit

beats.text: Tidal friction is draining its orbital energy, shrinking its year by milliseconds annually.
beats.visual: Telescopio Nazionale Galileo at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, La Palma
queries: Telescopio Nazionale Galileo Roque de los Muchachos
Roque de los Muchachos Observatory La Palma

beats.text: Within three million years, its star will completely consume this pitch-black world.
beats.visual: Artist concept of an exoplanet being consumed by its parent star
